selection_reason: F_competition has plateaued: CP-SAT at 1 s and 3 s both returned FEASIBLE 63.0 s with the same 51.0 s bound, and RL medium-seed-0 returned a worse 65.0 s. Further spend there is poor value. G_dual_bottleneck has no incumbent and a different nominal bottleneck (CLEAN, with CLEAN and RINSE both at 56.0 s nominal load), so it is the most informative untried scenario. A bottleneck-rule probe is the cheapest available method and establishes a verified baseline for the cross-scenario method comparison the objective requires, while testing whether rule policies transfer across scenario structure.

G_dual_bottleneck has only a rule baseline (199.0 s, ~3.55x the 56.0 s nominal lower bound) with 78.0 s chamber blocking and monotonically increasing wafer waiting, indicating robot serialization dominates under the rule policy. CP-SAT is the cheapest method that can jointly optimize transfer ordering and blocking. The untried CP budget for this scenario is 1 s (estimated ~4 s wall), well within the remaining wall budget (~537 s) and remaining CP search budget (56 s). This tests whether the rule baseline is far from optimal.

G_dual_bottleneck has a verified CP-SAT incumbent of 183.0 s (round-006), improved from the 199.0 s bottleneck-rule baseline (round-005), but the 1 s run returned FEASIBLE with a 41.0 s gap to its own 142.0 s bound after only ~27.7k branches. The next untried CP budget for this scenario is 3 s, which is cheap relative to the remaining wall budget (525 s) and remaining CP search budget (55 s), and directly isolates whether the gap is search-limited or encoding-limited on the same model before switching methods.

G_dual_bottleneck has a verified CP-SAT incumbent of 183.0 s (round-006). Round-007 showed that tripling the budget from 1 s to 3 s produced no change in incumbent or bound despite roughly doubling search effort (branches 27743 to 54762, conflicts 1770 to 8596), so small CP increments appear uninformative. The next untried CP budget of 10 s is the cheapest remaining probe that substantially increases search effort and directly tests whether the 41.0 s gap to the 142.0 s bound is search-limited at all. It is cheap relative to the remaining wall budget (about 510 s) and remaining CP search budget (52 s), and isolates search-time effects on the same encoding before considering a different method.

Both scenarios now have CP-SAT OPTIMAL proofs (F=63s, G=183s), so makespan cannot be improved. Remaining research value is in the secondary objective: tool cost. Round-010 showed the adaptive rule on F reached 65s at 0.35s tool time (cost ratio 0.16 vs incumbent), i.e. near-optimal makespan at a fraction of CP-SAT cost. The adaptive rule has never been tested on G_dual_bottleneck, where the only rule tried is bottleneck (199s). Testing adaptive on G probes whether the cheap rule generalizes across bottleneck topologies.
